A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Prompt Depth Anything work, with matching core methods, equations and experiments. All supplied pages are readable. V4 includes Appendices A–E; v3 ends with references without an appended supplement.

before.justification: V3 reports original depth-estimation, completion, reconstruction, ablation and robotic-grasping results in Tables I–VIII and accompanying figures.

after.justification: V4 reports original depth-estimation, reconstruction, ablation and grasping results in Tables 1–5, with additional empirical findings in its supplement.

M1.justification: V4 removes v3 Section III-D's pattern-agnostic method: serialized depth-point tokens, joint image/depth self-attention, positional encoding and associated median-depth normalization. The original convolutional prompt fusion, synthetic/real training pipeline and edge-aware loss remain.

E1.justification: V4 omits the six-benchmark random-point completion suite covering NYUv2, ScanNet, DIODE, ETH3D, KITTI and Waymo, and the DTU/Replica SfM evaluations. HyperSim, ARKitScenes, ScanNet++, grasping and qualitative vehicle-LiDAR testing remain, so outdoor coverage is not eliminated. The supplement also reports SHIFT/human-synthetic training and a dynamic-human reconstruction demonstration.

E2.justification: V4 removes comparisons with Marigold-DC, Omni-DC and PriorDepthAnything, and the SfM/MVS comparisons involving methods such as COLMAP, IGEV-MVS and Murre. It adds Depth Anything v1 to the ARKitScenes table and a BPNet vehicle-LiDAR comparison in Figure 16. Most retained core comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The 1,500-point completion protocol, DTU/Replica SfM reconstruction protocols, and 30×40-depth versus 1,200-point strategy test disappear. V4 adds a 512p–2160p resolution comparison and a combined-ControlNet control. Shared benchmark splits and training budgets remain unchanged; newly supplied implementation settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V3's cross-pattern prompting-strategy ablation in Table VII is removed. V4 adds resolution sensitivity, frame-resampling comparisons, combined-ControlNet testing and policy-initialization findings. The original architecture/data/loss ablations remain, and the Depth Pro ablation moves from Table VI to supplementary Table 5.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V4's newly disclosed robot-trajectory counts describe collected data, not repeated-run statistics.

E6.justification: The shared benchmark, retained ablation and grasping scores are unchanged, including ScanNet++ Ours L1 0.0250 and F-score 0.7619. V3's completion, DTU/Replica and strategy-comparison results disappear. V4 adds the ARKitScenes Depth Anything v1 row, supplementary qualitative findings and a ControlNet-combination comparison reporting F-scores of 0.730 versus 0.731.

T1.justification: The DPT formulation and loss Equations (1)–(2) remain unchanged. V4 Tables 6–7 spell out standard formulas for already-used evaluation metrics; they do not introduce new theoretical results. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V4 removes the pattern-agnostic contribution, the abstract's eight-zero-shot-benchmark claim and the introduction's SfM/MVS contribution without further fine-tuning. Its claims focus on the original LiDAR-prompted 4K method, ARKitScenes/ScanNet++ performance and downstream applications.

C2.justification: V4 removes explanations of failure on irregular sparse patterns, the need for two complementary prompting strategies and the broader SfM interpretation. Its supplement adds qualifications about simulated LiDAR noise, synthetic-data diversity and the ControlNet cost-benefit tradeoff. The long-range and temporal-flickering limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B–E supply frame-selection rules, ZipNeRF computation costs, dataset-specific losses, TSDF settings, baseline and RANSAC details, vehicle-LiDAR KNN preprocessing, and robot/policy specifications. These substantially expand reproducibility information without proving changes to retained procedures. Access statements also shift from explicit GitHub code availability to a project link and promised processed-data release.

R1.justification: V4 drops the CVPR-extension positioning and substantial recent-work discussion, including Depth Anything 3, Pixel-Perfect Depth, InfiniDepth and LingBot-Depth, alongside the completion/SfM comparison context. Supplementary citations add SAM2, SHIFT, Function4D and ResNet. The original distinction from Depth Prompting remains.

P1.justification: The extension-centered narrative becomes a narrower main paper followed by extensive discussion, results and implementation appendices. The title, authorship block, abstract and contribution list change, and the Depth Pro discussion moves into the supplement. Much shared method prose is retained, but the overall explanatory structure changes substantially.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted: Figure 1 moves to the opening page, shared result figures are regrouped, and Depth Pro rows become supplementary Table 5. V3's pattern-prompting, completion and DTU displays disappear. V4 adds Figures 9–16 and metric-definition Tables 6–7.

improvement.justification: V4 improves reproducibility through its detailed supplement and retains the principal benchmark results, while narrowing claims consistently with its scope. It also removes v3's tested pattern-agnostic mechanism, controlled applicability comparison and broader completion/SfM evidence. The transparency gains and loss of a supported technical contribution create a material tradeoff without a reliably assessable net quality direction.
